           │ and only opens these gates after the train has sent a signal indicating that it crossed the road. The requirement that should be met by the control   │
           │ system is that the gates are always closed when the train is crossing the road. The complete system consists of the three components Train, Gate, and │
           │ Controller: Train || Gate || Controller.  Model this system. You can assume that all trains pass the relevant track section in the same direction.    │
           │ Detail: The states of the transition system for the Train have the following intuitive meaning: in state "far" the train is not close to the          │
           │ crossing, in state "near" it is approaching the crossing and has just sent a signal to notify this, and in state "in" it is at the crossing. The      │
           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │
           │ train is approaching, from state 1 to 2 when the gate is lowering, from state 2 to 3 when the train is exiting the crossing, and from state 3 to 0    │
           │ when the gate is raising. The state changes of the Controller stand for handshaking with the trains (via the actions approach and exit) and the Gate  │
           │ (via the actions lower and raise via which the Controller causes the gate to close or to open, respectively). Use the variable names train_state,     │
           │ controller_state and gate_state. [Hint 1] Consider emphasizing the sequence of state transitions in the requirement specification. Add a precise      │

           │ gate state. Emphasize that the controller must transition from state 0 to 1 only when a train approaches (from 'far' to 'near'), and from state 2 to  │

           │ Detail: The states of the transition system for the Train have the following intuitive meaning: in state "far" the train is not close to the          │

           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │
           │ train is approaching, from state 1 to 2 when the gate is lowering, from state 2 to 3 when the train is exiting the crossing, and from state 3 to 0    │

           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │

           │   var train_state: enum { far, in, near };                                                                   │
           │   var controller_state: enum { 0, 1, 2, 3 };                                                                 │
           │   var gate_state: enum { down, up };                                                                         │
           │                                                                                                              │
           │   input train_approach: boolean;                                                                             │
           │   input train_exit: boolean;                                                                                 │
           │                                                                                                              │
           │   output gate_raise: boolean;                                                                                │
           │                                                                                                              │
           │   procedure step()                                                                                           │
           │     modifies controller_state;                                                                               │
           │     modifies gate_raise;                                                                                     │

           │       controller_state = 1;                                                                                  │

           │       controller_state = 2;                                                                                  │

           │       controller_state = 3;                                                                                  │

           │   }                                                                                                          │

           │ Detail: The states of the transition system for the Train have the following intuitive meaning: in state "far" the train is not close to the          │
           │ crossing, in state "near" it is approaching the crossing and has just sent a signal to notify this, and in state "in" it is at the crossing. The      │
           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │
           │ train is approaching, from state 1 to 2 when the gate is lowering, from state 2 to 3 when the train is exiting the crossing, and from state 3 to 0    │
           │ when the gate is raising. The state changes of the Controller stand for handshaking with the trains (via the actions approach and exit) and the Gate  │
